title: React Module 04 Core Check
description: Check your understanding of rendering elements, the virtual DOM, reconciliation, keys, lists, and conditional rendering.
author: DailyCoder

options.text: A description of what should appear in the UI
A real DOM node created by hand

questions.explanation: React elements are lightweight descriptions used by React to build and update the UI.

questions.prompt: What is the HTML mount point commonly used for?

options.text: The DOM node where React attaches the app

questions.explanation: React renders the root component into a DOM container such as an element with id `root`.

options.text: React comparing element trees to decide what changed

questions.explanation: During reconciliation, React diffs the previous and next descriptions to decide updates.

questions.prompt: Which statements about keys are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Keys help React track item identity in lists
Stable IDs usually make good keys
Keys should be unique among siblings
Keys are visible as normal props in the child automatically

questions.explanation: Keys identify sibling list items for reconciliation. They are not passed as ordinary props.

questions.prompt: Components should be pure while rendering and avoid causing side effects in the render body.
questions.explanation: Render should calculate UI from inputs; side effects belong in events or effects.

questions.prompt: Which is a common way to render an array of items?

options.text: Use `.map()` to return an element for each item

questions.explanation: React commonly renders lists by mapping data to elements.

questions.prompt: Which conditional rendering pattern can render no UI for a component?
questions.explanation: Returning `null` tells React to render nothing for that component.

questions.prompt: Which can cause unnecessary or confusing list behavior? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Using array indexes as keys for reorderable items
Using random keys that change every render
Using stable item IDs as keys
Omitting keys for sibling list items

questions.explanation: Unstable, missing, or index keys for changing lists can break identity tracking.
